question.text: If the equal sides <math><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></math> and <math><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi></math> (each equal to <math><mn>5</mn></math> units) of a right-angled isosceles triangle <math><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></math> are produced to <math><mi>P</mi></math> and <math><mi></mi><mi>Q</mi></math> such that <math><mi>B</mi><mi>P</mi><mo>.</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>A</mi><msup><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></math> then the line <math><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi></math> always passes through the fixed point (where <math><mi>A</mi></math> is the origin and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi></math> lie along the positive <math><mi>x</mi></math> and positive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math>-axis respectively)

solution.text:
Let, AP=h, AQ=k

Equation of the line PQ is xh+yk=1 … 1
Given, BP.CQ=AB2
⇒h-5k-5=25
or, 5h+5k=hk
or, 5h+5k=1
From 2, it follows that line 1, i.e., PQ passes through the fixed point 5,5
